title: A PLEASING AROMA FROM A SIN OFFERING

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'"They shall remove all the fat, just as the fat is removed from the fellowship offering, and the priest shall burn it on the altar as an aroma pleasing to the LORD. In this way the priest will make atonement for them, and they will be forgiven."'" - Lev 4:31 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is a phrase that should stop us: an aroma pleasing to the LORD — attached to a sin offering.

We first met that phrase over the burnt offering and the grain offering, offerings of devotion and thanksgiving. Now it appears over an offering brought because someone failed.

What pleases God about a sin offering? Not the sin. What pleases God is a sinner dealing honestly with sin His way. Confession pleases God. Repentance pleases God. A person walking to the altar rather than away from it pleases God.

Luke records Jesus saying there is rejoicing in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner who repents (Lk 15:10). Heaven does not sigh when you confess. Heaven celebrates.

That reframes repentance entirely. Most of us experience confession as a grim, embarrassed transaction we would rather get over with quickly. But God receives it as fragrance.

And the verse ends where the others ended: they will be forgiven. Third time in the chapter.

The next time you come to God with a failure, remember what He smells. Not your sin — the sweet aroma of a child coming home.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I experience confession as shameful, or as something God receives with pleasure?
2. What would change if I believed heaven rejoices when I repent?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that my honest confession is not disgusting to You but pleasing. Draw me quickly to You whenever I fall. Amen.
